Khalsa Primary is a Sikh faith school in a brand new building set in beautiful surroundings. We are a two form entry primary school catering for pupils from Nursery to Year 6.
At the core of the school is our belief that 'together we shine'. Our strength lies in our community and we place great emphasis on including not only the children in our care, but their parents and families and the general public too. We know that these community values feed through to above average academic results, and shape children with deeply embedded spiritual and social values.
Ms PK Sehmi, Headteacher

Follow Khalsa Primary
We are very proud of our academic results. In the summer of 2025 85% of our pupils attained the expected standard in reading, 83% in writing and 91% in maths, all of which are higher than the national averages.
SEE HOW OUR RESULTS COMPARE WITH NATIONAL AND LOCAL AVERAGES
The principles of Sikhism inform everything we do at Khalsa Primary. Our three Golden Rules are based on the teachings of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of our religion. With daily prayer and regular celebrations of Sikh festivals, children are given a grounding in spiritual understanding to sustain them through their lives.
Our children benefit from regular visits and events at Gurdwara Sri Guru Singh Saba in Southall, with whom we have close ties.
READ MORE ABOUT FAITH AT KHALSA PRIMARY
Sewa means 'selfless service' and is an integral part of the Sikh faith, and of life at Khalsa Primary. Our children have many opportunities to perform sewa in and around the local community. Our litter picking teams regularly venture out into Norwood Park to help tidy it up, and our children help the lunchtime staff by clearing plates and helping younger children in the dining hall.
You can keep up to date with what our sewadars have been up to by following us on Twitter and Instagram, and subscribing to our newsletter.
READ MORE ABOUT SEWA AT KHALSA PRIMARY
We are always available to show you around the school and demonstrate why a place at Khalsa Primary School is such a good start to your child's educational journey. Jaspreet Pooni in the school office is available to give you any advice you might need and to answer any questions you may have. We look forward to meeting you and your children and to welcoming you into our community.
APPLY FOR A PLACE AT KHALSA PRIMARY SCHOOL
Khalsa Primary School is situated in the quiet neighbourhood of Norwood Green and our children are within walking distance of the beautiful parkland at Osterley House, waterways such as the Brent Canal and are also a short journey from busy town centres like Hounslow and Southall.
We are extremely lucky to have a wonderful building which is set in a quiet and beautiful corner of London. We moved into our purpose built school in 2009 and our children, families and staff enjoy the use of bright open spaces indoors, inviting classrooms and communal spaces such as our Darbar Sahib and main hall which is used for P.E, lunches, assemblies and faith celebrations.
READ MORE ABOUT OUR FACILITIES
Privacy Overview

Welcome to Khalsa Primary
Khalsa Primary is a Sikh faith school which opened in 2009. We moved to our brand new, purpose built building in 2010. We are a two form entry primary school in the London Borough of Ealing and cater for pupils from Nursery to Year 6. The school is set in beautiful parkland and has excellent facilities.
As we are a relatively new school, always growing and developing, there is a great atmosphere of excitement. The children love coming to school and parents are eager to help and support us. As a result, we continue to develop and improve at a good pace. Staff and governors are skilled and knowledgeable and share our commitment so that the school provides an excellent education for all our children.
At Khalsa Primary we follow an enhanced and enriched version of the National Curriculum. As we are a Sikh faith school, we teach Sikh and Punjabi Studies and both subjects are taught by specialist staff. Within the school, there is a Sikh ethos which permeates all aspects of our work and is based on respect, caring, sharing and working hard to achieve the best.
The children and their achievements are at the heart of everything that we do. We are determined that all our pupils develop a love of learning and receive an excellent education. They are taught by a team of hard working and committed staff who have high expectations and believe that the children deserve the very best from our school.
Ms P K Sehmi, Headteacher
Privacy Overview

Faith at Khalsa Primary
We teach children about their religion and others, encourage them to ask questions and explore the ideas and teachings. Children take part in Sikh Studies lessons throughout their time at Khalsa, learning about the major figures, stories and morals from our past which are kept alive by Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.
We offer children the unique opportunity to take part in celebrations throughout the year. Children are able to perform seva such as reading Hukumnama or Ardas as part of celebrations which include the whole school community.
Naam Japo - Remembering God
We begin every day in the Darbar Sahib, praying, thinking about god and preparing our minds for the day. We keep Waheguru in our minds all day through our work and play.
Kirat Karo - Working Hard
We have high expectations of our children at all times in school. Our staff is dedicated to making sure that children work hard and achieve their potential. Children are taught about concepts like honesty, truthfulness and kindness.
Vand Chhako - Caring and Sharing
Our expectations of children extend beyond the classroom; we have a large focus on our behaviour, how we interact with others and reflecting on our behaviour and actions. We expect children to be empathetic, considerate and helpful to others.
Privacy Overview

Our Vision
We will ensure that our children have the best educational experience it is possible to have and, as a result, are fully prepared for life beyond our school. We want our children to understand their faith, to articulate their values and to be able to act in a way which reflects these. Our school is at the heart of the community which it serves; we create children who are ready to contribute and improve themselves, those around them and the places we live.
Our Values
'Khalsa' means the community of Sikhs. We use the word as an acronym to explain our school's ethos.
Knowledge
Khalsa Primary School provides all children with a broad, balanced and vibrant curriculum based on the National Curriculum. We teach children about, and encourage them to act in line with, both British values and the values inherent in the Sikh faith.
We ensure this by rigorously monitoring, reviewing and revising teaching across the curriculum to make sure it is well-planned, engaging and inclusive for all.
Harmony
The school is committed to maintaining harmonious relationships within the school and wider community. By building these positive relationships we endeavour to represent our community in a positive way.
We ensure this by developing and maintaining good relationships with all stakeholders through clear and effective communication.
Ambition
At our school, we have high expectations of our children and our staff. We aim to employ or develop outstanding practitioners, who are passionate about helping children to achieve their full potential. Our governing body provides robust, supportive and strategic leadership to develop this ambition.
We ensure this by maintaining effective teamwork, solution-focused approaches and always striving for the best.
Learning
Our community fosters an inclusive teaching and learning setting which is focused on the achievement of everyone. Numerous opportunities are provided for children, parents, governors and staff to learn and celebrate academic success.
We ensure this by having appropriately qualified and well-trained staff and governors with ongoing professional development mirroring their responsibilities.
Spiritual
The key tenets of the Sikh Faith are immersed in all aspects of school life: by working hard (Kirat Karna), sharing and caring (Vand Ke Shakna) and remembering God (Naam Japna), the school is able to demonstrate Sikh practice in everyday life.
We ensure this by incorporating spirituality in daily communal prayers in the Darbar Sahib, assemblies and special occasions where the whole community join together and celebrate. We reward children who follow the golden rules.
Achievement
At Khalsa we provide pupils and staff opportunities to achieve their full potential within a happy, caring, safe and secure environment.
We ensure this by recognising and celebrating achievement of everyone through relentless focus on pupil progress and attainment.

The aim is to build a sound base from which the children can develop in sport and in every aspect of their lives. In short the sports club can be related to as the ‘nursery school of sport.
The school uses the services of PSD, who provide a sports coach to teach PE as well as lead various sports clubs. The sports coach has an enthusiastic approach and has many years of experience and is attentive to the capabilities, needs and progress of our children:

Our Vision and Curriculum
We will ensure that our children have the best educational experience it is possible to have and, as a result, are fully prepared for life beyond our school. We want our children to understand their faith, to articulate their values and to be able to act in a way which reflects these. Our school is at the heart of the community which it serves; we create children who are ready to contribute and improve themselves, those around them and the places we live.
Our curriculum is designed to enable us to realise this vision. We have designed our curriculum ourselves, entirely to suit the needs and ambitions of our school community. In every subject, we have ensured that we have met the requirements of the National Curriculum. In most cases, we have exceeded these requirements in order to deliver on our school vision.
We have a strong focus on the progressive development of children’s knowledge and skills from Early Years to the end of Key Stage 2: our staff help children to understand and remember key ideas in every subject and to demonstrate their understanding through subject specific skills. Our curriculum is challenging for all, regardless of ability or needs. By the time they leave Khalsa, we expect children to be able to independently make links with different concepts they have learnt and to use their skills to answer enquiry questions.
To support children’s understanding, we have designed a curriculum that is rooted in experiences. Our curriculum has a strong focus on our own lives, experiences and local area. Themes such as local history, migration, Sikh and British values and our place in local and wider communities are present across different subjects. We make every effort to ensure that we provide context for learning through practical activities, off-site learning – for example at a museum – and relevant visitors to school.
Finally, we have a strong emphasis on outcomes which children can be proud of. Our curriculum is designed so that children are given the opportunity to demonstrate their understanding in a creative, evaluative or analytical way for every unit of work. Our staff have created learning journeys which answer key questions and allow children to produce excellent work.

Early Years Curriculum
Each child has an individual route to learning.
Teaching and learning will be based on the Early Years Foundation Stage Principles.
Teachers will plan and prepare learning opportunities so that every child receives an enjoyable and challenging learning and development experience that is tailored to meet their individual needs.
We will plan for development based on the four themes:
Your child’s teacher will value your child as a unique and special individual and the importance of each child’s individual route to learning.
They will use regular assessment to help your child progress and to plan and adapt further learning opportunities to suit your child’s needs.
All teachers will work with and involve parents to help us meet all children’s needs, learning styles and interests.
Sikh and Punjabi Studies
Nursery and Reception aged children will have tailored Sikh Studies and Punjabi Language lessons.
Reception aged children will participate daily in morning prayers.
Punjabi lessons will be taught appropriately according to the child’s age. A phonic system will be used and lessons tailored so that each child enjoys and participates.
Sikh Studies will provide opportunities for children to understand and learn about key elements of our Sikh Culture. This will include Gurbani (through history as well as music), History of Sikhism and Sikhi today. Again, this will be adapted to suit the needs of the child’s age and ability.
All lessons, learning and school life will be based on the Sikh ethos and values.
Adults working with your child
We are committed to safeguarding and promoting children’s welfare in all aspect. All adults working with children will have been previously thoroughly checked and assessed on their suitability.
All children and parents will feel safe and secure with all adults working at Khalsa Primary School.
For more information, please contact Ms P K Sehmi (Headteacher) or Ms J Butler (Deputy Headteacher) at the school.

Reading
Learning to read is a vital aspect of a child's education at primary level.
Phonics at Khalsa Primary School – an overview
We at Khalsa Primary School use ALS Phonics: Letters and Sounds scheme of work which provides a solid and continuous approach to the teaching of systematic synthetic phonics in Nursery, Reception and Key Stage 1. Validated by the Department for Education (DfE) and based on the principles of Letters and Sounds, it offers training, guidance and resources to support schools in the delivery of a successful and complete phonics programme.
It is split into 5 phases with the different phases being covered in different years in Foundation Stage & Key Stage 1.
The information below will give you an idea of what is expected at each level.
Phase 1- Lies mainly within the areas of communication and language and literacy within the Early Years Foundation Stage. It is the base for all subsequent phonic learning. Children will develop listening skills and phonological awareness in mainly adult-led activities, which will be consolidated and reinforced within the language-rich environment and child-initiated learning. This is underpinned by helping children to tune into sounds and discriminate between speech sounds. They will learn to alliterate the initial sound of words and blend and segment words orally.
Phase 2-Phonics teaches the children the phoneme-grapheme correspondence of the first 19 letters. Using these letters, children will learn to blend and segment and will learn to read vc and cvc words. At Phase 2, children will develop the skill of writing words or making words with magnetic letters/tiles with these initial graphemes.
Phase 3-Introduces 25 new graphemes, including some long vowels. These graphemes consist of consonant diagraphs (ch, sh, ng), vowel diagraphs (ai, ee, oa) and vowel trigraphs (igh, air, ear). Children will learn to blend these graphemes for reading in one-syllable and two-syllable words. During Phase 3, children will practise writing and making words with consonant digraphs, vowel diagraphs and vowel trigraphs. Children will also learn to read and write captions and sentences with these letters. A rhyming element has also been incorporated into the Phase 3 long vowel lesson plan to ensure that all children can recognise and generate rhyming words by the end of Reception.
Phase 4-Is to consolidate children’s knowledge of phonemes and graphemes in the reading and writing of words of increasing length and complexity containing short vowels, long vowels and adjacent consonants. No new graphemes are introduced at this stage. Children will practise previously learnt graphemes and learn to blend and segment words with increasing automaticity. As children become more proficient in their blending and segmenting of polysyllabic words, their confidence and independence as a reader will grow too. At Phase 4, children continue to learn to read and write sentences using one or more high-frequency words, words of varying length and complexity and words containing adjacent consonants.
Phase 5-Is where children broaden their knowledge of graphemes and phonemes to apply in their reading and writing. They will learn new graphemes for graphemes they already know and will learn alternative pronunciation for some graphemes they have learnt previously.
During Phase 5, children will learn to read words with alternative pronunciation of graphemes and words with two and three syllables. Children will learn to choose the appropriate grapheme when writing words and learn to write two-syllable words, three-syllable words and polysyllabic words.

Remote learning and Google Classroom
How to hand in homework on Google Classroom
http://www.khalsaschool.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/handinwork.mp4
All of our homework is given and sent back through our virtual learning environment, Khalsa School At Home. We use Google Classroom to communicate, set work, post useful materials and feedback to children on work they have been doing. All spellings, times tables and other homework tasks will be given out through Google Classroom.
Every child in our school has their own unique login which will take them to their class where they can see the work which is has been set, ask questions and receive feedback from teachers. It is very important that children and parents log in regularly to check what messages and work are available.
Although it is possible to access Google Classroom through a smartphone, we recommend that children do so by using a tablet or laptop.
If you have issues, please read the guide or watch some of the videos below.
For any further issues or require login details, please contact the school.
